scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: Tatkal opens at ten AM, and within minutes, the seats are gone. What happens in those minutes?

scenes.name: open
scenes.text: Tatkal booking opens one day before the journey. At ten for AC classes, and eleven for non AC.

scenes.name: rush
scenes.text: Huge numbers of people log in and hit book at the exact same second. That's a massive spike for any server.

scenes.name: queue
scenes.text: So requests are queued, and checks like captcha and login verification slow down bots, and spread out the load.

scenes.name: seat
scenes.text: When you submit, the system checks the live seat count for that train and class, and reserves one while you pay.

scenes.name: pay
scenes.text: If your payment fails or times out, the ticket isn't booked, and that seat goes back for the next person.

scenes.name: quota
scenes.text: Tatkal is only a small share of seats on each train. With that much demand, it can sell out in minutes.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Window, queue, seat, payment. A race for a few seats. Follow for more on how things really work.
